proposals.evidence: Dhakal p. 67 prints /pʰar/ “blade,” the second source token of the form linked from p. 53 in pass161. Turner9052 section 2 gives Punjabi pharhā “blade, nib,” selecting the rhotic *phara- branch over section 1 phal-.

proposals.evidence: Dhakal p. 67 prints /ṭu.ri.ke/ “break.” Turner6079 gives Bengali tuṛā “to break,” Kumaoni ṭoṛṇo and regional toṛ-/tuṛ- verbs; the Darai rhotic distinguishes this branch from Turner6065 ṭuṭ- “be broken.” The source does not specify transitivity, so the rhotic form is the decisive match.
